Making Waves — canonical program record

Status: Proposed project programming / professional-resource integration

1. Purpose

Making Waves is a 50 Ways listening and demonstration format about how signals interact and how deliberate listening can reveal what changed.

The project record is an original programming layer. It is not a reproduction of Producer Dojo course material, newsletter copy, lesson files, recordings, branding, or other proprietary material.

2. Source / reference boundary

Producer Dojo / ill.Gates is documented here as a professional resource whose public educational ecosystem is relevant to the subject.

The source layer may inform the project's research and programming. Any protected source material remains outside the public repository unless permission establishes otherwise.

Rule: source attribution is not a license.

The project should use its own language, demonstrations, examples, sequencing, visual treatment, exercises, and event production.

3. Core learning experience

The audience hears the behavior before being given a recipe.

Demonstration sequence

  1. Hear It — hear two signals separately.
  2. Add It — hear them together and compare the combined result.
  3. Change It — alter one signal or its polarity and listen for the difference.
  4. Isolate It — demonstrate a controlled comparison that exposes what changed.
  5. Apply It — use a production tool or process and listen specifically for its audible effect.
  6. Name It — explain the underlying audio concept after the listener has heard it.
  7. Transfer It — connect the listening method to creative decision-making beyond the demonstration.

The exact audio assets should be original project assets or separately cleared materials.

5. Live event format

Format: listening lab + demonstration + facilitated discussion

Suggested run of show:

  • Opening: establish the listening question.
  • Demonstration A: separate signals.
  • Demonstration B: combined signals.
  • Demonstration C: controlled polarity/processing change.
  • Audience A/B: ask what changed before naming the technique.
  • Discussion: move from audible behavior to production decision.
  • Application: audience identifies a change in a new example.
  • Closing: document the takeaway and point to the learning materials.

Event production controls

Before public performance or recording:

  • identify all audio/music assets;
  • clear third-party recordings and compositions as applicable;
  • obtain presenter/performer permissions;
  • obtain participant release/recording permissions where required;
  • clear venue and event-media requirements;
  • confirm brand/name/logo permissions for any co-branded use;
  • document whether the event is educational, promotional, paid, licensed, or sponsored;
  • preserve the final run of show and asset list.
